classification.difficultyReason: Convert a contextual threshold to a z-score, identify the empirical-rule tail and calculate an expected number of refunds.

content.prompt: Nathan sells a diet plan with a money-back guarantee if the customer does not lose 9 kg in the first three months. The weight loss after three months is normally distributed with a mean loss of 13.2 kg and a standard deviation of 1.4 kg.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the z-score corresponding to a weight loss of 9 kg?

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage of customers will not reach the 9 kg in three months?

answer.worked:
A loss of 9 kg is three standard deviations below the mean. By the empirical rule, approximately $99.7\%$ of customers lose between 9 kg and 17.4 kg. The two tails are equal, so the percentage losing less than 9 kg is
$$\frac{100\%-99.7\%}{2}=0.15\%.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Nathan has sold 2000 diet plans. How many refunds are expected?

spec.description: Authored solution sketch following the normal-curve method taught on page 28; the lower tail below 9 kg is shaded.
spec.mathematics: Mean 13.2 kg, standard deviation 1.4 kg; 9 kg corresponds to z=-3. Empirical-rule lower-tail area is approximately 0.15%.

sizing.exceptionReason: Seven decimal raw-score ticks need horizontal separation at their retained native label size.
